name: Joel Corcoran

bio.statement: Corcoran's voters' pamphlet statement lists his background as a small business and nonprofit attorney.
Corcoran's pamphlet statement lists BS and MS degrees from Oregon State University and a JD from the University of Oregon School of Law.
bio.excerpt: Oregon State University, B.S., M.S.; University of Oregon School of Law, J.D.

bio.statement: Corcoran's pamphlet statement lists prior work as policy counsel for the Portland City Council and as state counsel and constituent service director in the U.S. Senate.
bio.excerpt: Policy Counsel (Portland City Council); State Counsel, Constituent Service Director (U.S. Senate)

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Corcoran owns a public interest law firm called Reluctant Cynic Legal Services.
bio.excerpt: Corcoran is a lawyer who owns a public interest firm called Reluctant Cynic Legal Services.

positions.statement: Corcoran's voters' pamphlet statement calls for independent legal and budget offices to ensure balanced oversight.
positions.excerpt: Establish independent legal and budget offices to ensure balanced oversight

positions.statement: Corcoran's pamphlet statement calls for a transparent, unified budget process with monthly review sessions.
positions.excerpt: Modernize our convoluted budget process into a transparent, unified system with regular monthly review sessions

positions.statement: Corcoran's pamphlet statement calls for auditing city contracts and setting guidelines for when work is done in-house.
positions.excerpt: Audit city contracts to eliminate waste, establish clear guidelines for when to perform work in-house

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Corcoran says expanding public utility options can restore household affordability.
positions.excerpt: We can restore household affordability by expanding public utility options

positions.statement: Corcoran's pamphlet statement calls for abolishing ICE.
Corcoran's pamphlet statement pledges to defend BIPOC, queer and trans people.
positions.excerpt: Defend BIPOC, queer, and trans folks.

positions.statement: OPB reports Corcoran wants to improve the city's new form of government in its early years.
positions.excerpt: He wants to improve the city’s new form of government in its nascent years.

gaps: No voting record (has not held elected office)

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report.
